runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Soft last time but Ben Haslam's yard is 0 wins from 21 in the last 14 days — Andrew Mullen booked, and stepping up to 6f on Good to Firm is an unknown, though the recent third on Good ground is encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out following third- and fourth-placed efforts before that, and has raced over today's trip before. His trainer is out of form, though — no winners from 21 runners in the last fortnight — leaving him only fifth on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Furturra

runners_data.name: Boleto

runners_data.comment: Boleto was unplaced last time out, having won two starts back, and is already proven over today's trip and going. Fit again after 24 days, he's only seventh on our figures here and needs to find more to feature.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's second string in the race, held up and the only true hold-up horse in the field — three runs on Good ground with a placed effort at 6f are the key positives, but in a race likely to be run at a sustainable pace, getting competitive from the back is a stiff task; Ben Robinson stays aboard.|

runners_data.name: Brandenburg
runners_data.note: Returned from 68 days off to win over 5f Soft on debut before a distant 12th on Soft again — stepping up to 6f on Good to Firm is a major unknown, and while Joanna Mason claims, Stephen Hanlon's yard is 1/13 in 14 days; a natural prominent type who will struggle to secure that spot here.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having been unplaced in the run before that, but he hasn't run since — a 68-day absence. Already proven over today's trip, he sits bottom of our figures in this field, leaving plenty to find fresh off a lengthy break.

races.paceDynamic: Super Tuscan is the one confirmed front-runner here, and on Good to Firm ground at York over 6f she is expected to stride on from the gates and control the tempo without being seriously pressured from outside. With only one genuine pace-setter in the field, the tempo is likely to be honest but manageable rather than searching, which typically sets up a strong-travelling prominent horse well on this straight, unforgiving track. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate — Boleto, Ballisty, and Brandenburg are all natural prominent horses redistributed to midfield on the map because Super Tuscan is first to that position and there is simply no room for all of them to race where they want; of the three, Boleto (Clive Cox, Rossa Ryan) and Furturra (proven course-and-distance form) are most likely to actually press into a prominent spot. This race shape — a controlled, single-pacemaker lead — favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first two or three immediately behind the leader and sprint off a genuine but not brutal gallop, particularly those with strong recent form on Good to Firm-equivalent going at 6f.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Super Tuscan sets a manageable tempo unchallenged and one or two prominent runners travel fluently behind before kicking clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Super Tuscan dictates from the front while Furturra or Big Cigar sits in the slipstream, and the Good to Firm ground ensures the gallop is honest but never punishing, allowing a well-placed runner to produce a clean sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Super Tuscan sets a slow-to-moderate early gallop and the redistributed prominent types fail to press on, leaving the front two to coast home.
scenarios.body: A dawdling early pace would suit a runner with tactical speed who can switch off and then quicken sharply over the final two furlongs on fast ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Best Traveller Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Boleto, Ballisty, or Brandenburg force their way into prominent positions and the early stages become fractious and competitive, elevating the tempo.
scenarios.body: A messy, contested early pace would stretch the field sooner and could bring one of the more resolute types — particularly Furturra with her repeated 6f Good ground form — into play strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage produces a genuinely fast early gallop that burns off the front-runners, leaving the race open for a hold-up finisher.
scenarios.body: Rbflying, the sole true hold-up horse, would benefit most from an unusually fast pace that ties up those who raced prominently, though this scenario is unlikely given the single confirmed pacemaker and that closers are thin on the ground here.

watchPoints.text: Super Tuscan's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the hinge of this race — if Boleto or Brandenburg press her hard into the first two furlongs, the pace dynamic shifts dramatically and the front two could tire, opening the race for a prominent closer like Furturra.

Boleto's previous run (19th at Goodwood) came on Good ground over the same trip — if that run conceals a physical issue or unsuitable draw, Rossa Ryan may not be able to push into the expected prominent position, which would change the shape materially.

Brandenburg's 68-day absence and previous form entirely on Soft ground is a concern on Good to Firm at York — Joanna Mason will need to place her perfectly if she is to make any impact, and a slowly-away start could leave her at the back against her natural prominent style.

Furturra's trainer Tim Easterby runs two horses in this race (Furturra and Rbflying) — watch for market moves between the pair in the final hour, as stable support will indicate which the yard considers the better prospect here.|

The Good to Firm going at York on this card is relevant to any horse whose best form has come on softer surfaces — Social Spirit (5f Good) and Brandenburg (both wins/places on Soft) face a meaningful ground question that should be factored into assessment.|

runners_data.comment: Two wins from his last five starts, including one two starts back, underline him as a leading threat, and he's proven over today's trip and going before. Third on our figures, though a modest speed figure alongside is the one small concern.

runners_data.comment: A win earlier in his last six starts, sandwiched among more modest efforts, shows there's ability there, and he's proven over today's trip and going before. Fourth on our figures, the main concern is a stable currently just 3% in-form over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has mostly contested longer trips — his last five all came at 10f or 12f; dropping to 8f here is a significant trip reduction and though the going suits, he may find the race over before he's had time to engage.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, with only a sixth as the best of a modest sequence, though he has proven today's trip and going before. Ninth on our figures, there's little in the recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: The Lost King

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's hold-up type has done most of his work at 7f in Good to Soft/Good conditions; stepping up in trip here and while the class is right at OR 94, his sim-going record (6/9) is moderate and he needs things to fall perfectly from the back.

runners_data.comment: A win and a runner-up effort came early in his last five starts, but two blanks and a modest sixth last time out point to a fade since. Proven over today's trip and going before, and seventh on our figures, rediscovering that form after 47 days off is the ask.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell

runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, with a second the highlight but two sevenths in there too, and he's proven today's distance before. Tenth on our figures, a lengthy 36-day layoff adds to the questions over this modest sort.

runners_data.name: New Image

runners_data.note: The three-year-old from R Mike Smith's yard has form over 5f and 6f with wins in Soft; stepping to 8f on Good to Firm is a significant ask for a horse who hasn't stayed beyond 6f yet — a natural front-runner being squeezed back by the field's configuration makes this look a tough task.

races.paceDynamic: David Of Athens is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push him across the opening quarter-mile on York's straight mile, he should establish a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground — sustainable enough that he won't tie up but unlikely to be truly strong enough to burn off hold-up horses late. The field is, however, stacked with prominent-running types: First Principle, Mr Swivell, Bragbor, New Image, Gentle George and Cosi Fan Tutte are all natural front-rank runners who simply cannot all occupy that territory — several will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield berths, blunting their winning chances and creating a slightly messy, bunched mid-race dynamic. Cerulean Bay, The Lost King and Apiarist are equipped to race prominently in second rank and will likely fill the immediate chasing positions, meaning the race resolves into a searching last two furlongs with the front players carrying the tempo into the straight. This shape favours horses that can track the pace from a handy second or third position and sustain their effort through the dip — prominent-to-midfield closers with proven Good to Firm form at the trip hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If David Of Athens dictates an honest but uncontested pace and prominent chasers Cerulean Bay and The Lost King track him into the straight.
scenarios.body: David Of Athens sets a metronomic tempo that suits those racing just off him, and the final two furlongs on York's flat mile become a stamina-inflected sprint from the front pack. Horses who have settled just behind the leader without burning energy in traffic are ideally placed to collar him or hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Glut Causes Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of natural prominent types — First Principle, Mr Swivell, Gentle George — jostle for position and create a faster, uneven early pace.
scenarios.body: The increased early tempo stretches the field and creates a slightly stronger gallop than expected, meaning hold-up horses like Checkandchallenge and Khafiz get a genuine searching pace to aim at. Those with the class and Good to Firm form to close from further back pick up ground powerfully in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If David Of Athens is allowed to soft-pedal the early stages and the chasing pack misjudge the pace, leaving him clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: On a flat, fair track with Good to Firm underfoot, a well-positioned leader who hasn't over-exerted can prove very hard to reel in if the field dawdles before realising the danger. David Of Athens has won over this course and distance and the Jehani yard is capable of springing a surprise at big odds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Produce Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely fast, pressured pace develops and opens the race up for closers coming from well off the speed.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both the redistributed prominent horses to create significant early friction and the true hold-up horses — Checkandchallenge, Khafiz, Tuscan Hills — to find clear runs in the final quarter-mile, a combination of events that is possible but heavily dependent on circumstances breaking right. Their finishing kick on Good to Firm is moderate and the flat York track rarely delivers dramatic late swoops in a muddled-pace handicap.

watchPoints.text: David Of Athens is the sole front-runner and if Pierre-Louis Jamin gets a soft lead, the price on offer could be far shorter than his market position suggests — watch for any move to back him at big odds before the off.

The cluster of natural prominent types (First Principle, Mr Swivell, Bragbor, New Image, Gentle George) means the opening quarter-mile could become scrappy as they compete for positions they can't all fill — watch for a bumpy, faster-than-expected early pace that changes the complexion of the race entirely.

Gentle George has never raced beyond 6f and is stepping up to 8f on Good to Firm ground for the first time; if he attempts to lead or race very prominently and ties up turning into the straight, he becomes a serious interference risk for horses tracking him.

Checkandchallenge (hood, hold-up style) is likely to be last or near-last early — watch where Rossa Ryan positions him entering the straight, as York's flat run-in gives hold-up horses very little margin for a blocked run in a 13-runner field.

Tuscan Hills has dropped sharply in trip from 10-12f to 8f; watch his early pace — if he races too keenly without the longer distances to settle him, his stamina reserves won't compensate and he could fade in the final furlong when it matters most.

races.paceDynamic: American Affair is the one confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner field and, with no genuine rival to pressurise her early, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, self-controlled gallop from the stalls — conditions that suit a horse who can dictate tempo on Good to Firm ground over York's straight five. The pace is real but not savage; with only one horse willing to lead, the race shape is likely to be steady-to-moderate in the first furlong before she settles into a rhythm, meaning the race will be run on her terms from flag to roughly the two-furlong marker where the sprint home begins. This race shape structurally advantages horses who can travel prominently just off the pace — those able to track American Affair without wasting energy — rather than pure hold-up horses who will face a wall of rivals and a tempo that may not be fast enough to set them alight from the back. Several horses mapped to midfield — including Dickensian, Luna A Inbhir Nis, Revival Power, Lexington Blitz, Azure Angel, and Naana's Shadow — are natural prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred forward berth in a 15-runner field, and in practice it is Dickensian (strong recent form, Kevin Ryan stable in good nick) and Revival Power who look most likely to claim positions close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: American Affair Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If American Affair bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but controlled tempo, allowing the horse travelling closest to her to produce a strong late kick.
scenarios.body: American Affair's sustainable gallop creates a race where horses tracking in the first two or three positions carry minimum traffic risk and arrive at the two-furlong pole full of running; the prominent-placed horse who can quicken off that tempo wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, American Affair Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slower than expected and American Affair's rivals fail to pick her up in time, allowing her to steal first run into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With rivals sitting in a bunched group mid-pack and the tempo modest, American Affair's tactical lead gives her a break that may prove decisive on fast ground where the front is difficult to peg back; her OR=109 and solid good-ground record make this credible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Into Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If American Affair is outpaced or goes too slowly and the field concertinas entering the final furlong, producing a sprint from a pack.
scenarios.body: A mass-casualty finish with no clear leader favours horses with the freshest legs and a high TS ceiling who can produce a sharp late burst through a narrow gap; hold-up horses with tactical speed benefit most in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Held-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a truly fast early pace develops unexpectedly — perhaps from multiple prominent types forcing the issue — and genuine closers get a strong gallop to aim at.
scenarios.body: This shape is relatively unlikely given the clear dominance of one front-runner and the compressed midfield, but if the race is run at a high early clip, hold-up horses who can produce a sustained burst have a slim window; the redistribution of many nominally prominent types into midfield means they are not true closers and this shape is the least natural of the four.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dickensian or Revival Power — both natural prominent types — can break sharply enough to claim a forward position early, as their ability or failure to do so will define whether the pace scenario unfolds as projected.

American Affair's Paul Mulrennan must judge the opening fractions carefully; if he dawdles to conserve her, the field may swamp her before the furlong pole, but if he goes too hard she risks emptying before the line — monitor the early pace from the stalls.

Heavenly Heather's sim-going record of just 3 from 15 on comparable going is a stark concern on what appears to be fast ground; if conditions are riding faster than published, she may underperform her recent placed form significantly.

With six or more horses genuinely wanting to be prominent in a straight 5f sprint, watch for significant early crowding on the stands side — horses who draw wide and cannot be covered across early may lose ground before the race settles.

Naana's Shadow's upward form trajectory (three wins in last five at OR=91) makes her one to monitor if she can secure a forward position — her true style is prominent and she is competitive on class despite the lower rating.

races.name: John Smith's Cup (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Respond
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with solid recent form including two wins on similar ground; suited by this trip and the prominent stalking role, and Andrew Balding's stable is firing with a 14-day strike rate of 14/68; tongue-tie fitted and has course-suitable form.
runners_data.comment: Respond boasts two wins and three places from his last five starts, with today's trip and going already proven. Thirty-six days off, carrying 138lb from stall 20, he ranks fourth of 22 on our figures — needing more to reel in the pair rated above him.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, rated 105, trained by Gosden and partnered by Havlin; has a style-fit flag suggesting he is racing out of natural role at this trip, and his ability to truly set a good gallop over 1m2½f is the race's pivotal question — if he stops, all bets change.
runners_data.comment: Warrant Holder heads our figures, backed by two wins and three places from his last five starts and today's trip and going already proven. Fresh within three weeks, he carries 138lb from stall 9 — only his modest speed figure offers pause.

runners_data.name: Yabher
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained four-year-old returning from 70 days off; excellent form on similar fast ground with four wins from nine comparable-going starts; has scope to improve on his last run and travels well from a prominent position — the layoff is the only question mark.
runners_data.comment: Yabher has won three of his last five starts, including his latest two, and arrives with today's trip and going already proven. But a 70-day absence and a modest speed figure leave him only ninth of 22 on our figures from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Thunder Run
runners_data.note: Rated 103 but recent form figures of 40-720 are uninspiring; has won on good ground before but the five-year-old is stepping back from a modest run and Shane Gray takes over; the wide draw and patchy recent form make confidence difficult.
runners_data.comment: Thunder Run is without a win in his last five starts, mixing a runner-up effort with four modest finishes, though a strong speed figure of 98 puts him third of 22 on our figures. Proven over today's trip and going, his indifferent placings remain the risk.

runners_data.name: Danger Bay
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old arrives in excellent fettle with a hat-trick of wins on good ground and Tudhope in the saddle; races prominently and has the form profile to be competitive at the head of affairs, with a good-to-firm run record of 5 from 6.
runners_data.comment: Danger Bay has won three of his last five starts, including his latest, with only a well-beaten ninth breaking the run, and he steps out fresh after 47 days off. Proven over today's trip and going, he carries 135lb from stall 3 and rates seventh of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Will Scarlet
runners_data.note: Rated just 97 but has won twice on good and good-to-firm ground at this sort of trip; carried a headgear flag and the claim of Mason Paetel (5) could be a factor; has recently proven himself from a prominent position and the return to quicker ground looks ideal.
runners_data.comment: Will Scarlet has won twice in his last six starts, but a below-par ninth sits among the places, and he's only 16th of 22 on our figures. He does know today's trip, though, fresh from a run 16 days ago.

runners_data.name: Hand Of God
runners_data.note: Five-year-old trained by Harry Charlton who broke a run of defeats when winning last time on good ground; makes his appeal as a prominent racer on fast ground, though previous runs at 10f have been inconsistent and the step back up in company is a test.
runners_data.comment: Hand Of God struck last time out and rates a close second of 22 on our figures with a smart 93 speed figure. He's proven over today's trip and going, though the rest of his last five starts read modestly and this is his first run in 57 days.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bethune
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who won on good ground but has run below that level on his last visit; Rob Hornby takes over and, while headgear has been tried, the horse's prominent-to-hold-up blend makes him a player if the race becomes untidy in the pack.
runners_data.comment: Quai De Bethune won once in his last five starts, with two sixths among the rest of that form, and rates a fair fifth of 22 on our figures. He's fresh from 36 days off and already proven over today's trip and going, from stall 6 carrying 133lb.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Returning from 142 days off, which is a significant flag even with two wins on comparable ground; Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore yard has a modest 14-day strike rate and Tom Eaves rides; the long absence overshadows otherwise solid good-ground credentials.
runners_data.comment: Dain Ma Nut In has won twice in his last five starts, but three below-par efforts in between leave him down in 17th of 22 on our figures. A 142-day absence since his last run is the concern, though today's trip and going are already proven.

runners_data.name: Auld Toon Loon
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Tom Dascombe who is a genuine front-running type; the redistribution places him in midfield on the map because too many horses want that territory, meaning he will likely be less comfortable than usual — his style-fit score reflects the chance he races below his best.
runners_data.comment: Auld Toon Loon won once in his last five starts, but a seventh, a third, an eighth and an unplaced effort surround that success, leaving him a middling eighth of 22 on our figures. Fresh from 36 days off, he's already proven over today's trip and going from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Raammee
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has won twice on standard ground but his form is at shorter trips (8f); stepping up in distance here and, as a true prominent racer pushed into a midfield slot by the crowded shape, getting an easy lead position is far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Raammee won two of his last four starts before fading to fourth, but rallied for a narrow second last time out. He rates sixth of 22 on our figures, is fresh from a run 28 days ago, and carries 128lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Iron Fist
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's four-year-old has placed on good ground at 10f and is a naturally prominent runner; with the field overloaded at the front, Oisin Orr will face a choice between fighting for position or dropping back — his best form came when allowed to stride on.
runners_data.comment: Iron Fist won once in his last five starts and has returned to form of late. He was third last time out, with a runner-up run two starts back. He knows today's trip, is fresh from a run 49 days ago, and rates 11th of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Richard & Peter Fahey who wears a visor and has one win at this trip on good ground; at his best racing prominently, but with the race map forced to push him back, the Fahey yard's busy 14-day book (7/69) means a competitive entry is expected regardless.
runners_data.comment: Have Secret won once in his last five starts, three back, but was below that level either side and is unplaced most recently. He's proven over today's trip and going, fresh from a run 36 days ago, and rates tenth of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Believer
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose last win on good ground came over 10f but who has only hit the board in 1 from 15 on genuinely fast ground — a concerning stat; Paul Mulrennan rides and, while he is a prominent type, the going record is a major negative here.
runners_data.comment: Fantasy Believer won once in his last five starts, four back, but has faded since. He was fifth last time out, with an unplaced run and a sixth in between. He's proven over today's trip and going, fresh from a run 29 days ago, and rates 13th of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: James Owen-trained five-year-old who ran just seven days ago; has a solid record on good ground with two wins from nine comparable runs, and the quick turnaround is notable — the style displacement to midfield slightly compromises his best chance, which is from the front.
runners_data.comment: Sportingsilvermine won last time out and boasts two wins in his last six starts, but three of the others were well held including two unplaced efforts. Quick to back up just seven days later, he's proven over today's trip and going yet rates only 18th of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Oli Rix who has been winning at shorter distances (7f) and now steps up sharply to 1m2½f; form at this trip is absent and, while placed on good ground before, the jump in distance is a genuine question mark even accounting for the weight advantage.
runners_data.comment: Spell Master won three starts back but has dipped since. He was third last time out, with an eighth two starts back. He does know today's going, is fresh from a run 22 days ago, and rates 14th of 22 on our figures from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Fahey who is a genuine hold-up horse in the 88-rated band; recent form is patchy with a solitary runner-up from five starts on comparable ground, but his natural style is not compromised by the field shape — he is a true closer looking for late spoils.
runners_data.comment: Castle Stuart is without a win in his last five starts but found more last time out to finish runner-up, amid modest form that also included two sixths and a seventh. Proven over today's trip and going and fresh from a run 29 days ago, he rates 15th of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old ran just six days ago, which is a very quick turnaround; has shown consistent placed form on good ground at 10f but the redistribution to midfield is honest — he is a naturally prominent runner who may not get a clean run in a 22-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Altareq won last time out but that followed a modest sequence of three thirds and an unplaced effort, and he's rated down in 21st of 22 on our figures. Quick to back up just six days later, he is at least proven over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Nebula
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Richard & Peter Fahey claimed by Warren Fentiman (3) who is an inexperienced claimer; one win from 13 on good ground suggests the fast-ground angle is not reliable, and the jockey's claim may offset some weight but adds a tactical risk.
runners_data.comment: Rainbow Nebula won four starts back but has been below that level since, no better than fifth in his last three. He's proven over today's trip and going, fresh from a run 16 days ago, and rates 12th of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Salam Dubawi
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old ran six days ago and is a genuine hold-up type, meaning his style is not displaced by the crowded shape; one win on good ground at 9f but the step up in trip and quick turnaround from a recent race are concerns for this 87-rated runner.
runners_data.comment: Salam Dubawi has won twice in his last five starts, alternated with two unplaced efforts, and was only third last time out — leaving him bottom of the field on our figures. He's at least fresh from a run six days ago and proven over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has a previous headgear flag (p) and is a natural hold-up horse in a race where that style is not the dominant play; zero wins from 15 on comparable going is a stark statistic, though Duran Fentiman rides and Easterby has been active (15/112 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Per Contra remains without a win in his last six starts, with only a third his best effort among finishes that also include two outside the frame. He's proven over today's trip and going, fresh from a run 16 days ago, and rates 20th of 22 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old carries the lightest weight in the race and has recent good form including a win at 10f on good ground; Cam Hardie takes over, and as a naturally prominent type displaced to midfield by the field's crowding, he has ability but faces a stiff first handicap test.
runners_data.comment: Pearl River won twice in his last five starts and was a close second last time out, but the yard is out of form (3 winners from 57 runners, 5%, in the last fortnight) and he rates only 19th of 22 on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Warrant Holder is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-strong field and, with no genuine pressing rival likely to sit on his girth from the outset, he can control the tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at York. The 1m2½f trip on this flat, galloping track rewards horses who travel comfortably in a rhythm and produce a sustained effort from two furlongs out rather than a short, sharp burst, which suits a pace that is controlled rather than frantic. With an unusual concentration of horses who naturally want to race prominently — Auld Toon Loon, Raammee, Iron Fist, Have Secret, Fantasy Believer, Sportingsilvermine and others are all genuine prominent types who have been mapped to midfield purely because the race shape cannot accommodate them all — there will be significant crowding and competition for the first few positions behind Warrant Holder, creating a busy and potentially messy early-race dynamic. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly just off the pace in the first two groups and sustain their effort into the straight, meaning genuine stalking prominent-to-midfield types with good handicap form on fast ground are best placed, while true hold-up horses must hope the pace collapses sufficiently to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Warrant Holder Controls, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Warrant Holder sets a fair but not breakneck gallop and the prominent stalkers track him comfortably before engaging two out.
scenarios.body: Warrant Holder dictates at a sensible tempo, allowing the true prominent racers slotted just behind to conserve energy and deliver sustained runs from two furlongs out; on this flat, galloping track at 1m2½f, the horses who travel prominently and finish strongly are ideally suited to the shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Crowded Midfield Chaos, One Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent-type horses creates a congested and scrappy race behind the leader, forcing several into positions wider or further back than ideal.
scenarios.body: The competition for early prominence turns the first half-mile into a scrappy affair, with horses bumping and shuffling for slots; the winners in this shape are those with the ability to travel smoothly on the outside or switch off for a genuine late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Slows, Front Two Win
scenarios.trigger: If Warrant Holder and whoever slots in second set a crawl that turns the race into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A modest early tempo compresses the field and reduces the race to a quick-fire finish where positional advantage at the two-furlong pole is decisive; horses already on the pace who can quicken on fast ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Claim Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up those on the front end and create a true test of stamina over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop — perhaps driven by one of the redistributed prominent types pushing forward — burns off the stalkers and opens the door for genuine hold-up horses to swoop late; however, this shape is less likely given most of the apparent hold-up horses are displaced prominent types rather than natural closers.

watchPoints.text: Warrant Holder's gallop must be monitored from the off — if he crawls, the entire field will be restless and the race will become a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, radically changing which horses can win.

With at least eight horses who naturally want to race prominently and only space for two or three behind Warrant Holder, expect significant early crowding and possible interference in the first three furlongs as Auld Toon Loon, Raammee, Iron Fist and others jostle for position.
Yabher's 70-day absence is worth tracking in the market — William Haggas horses rarely need the run, but a drifting price on course would suggest connections are cautious about the layoff.
Fantasy Believer's going record — just 1 place from 15 on genuinely fast ground — is a red flag if the going remains on the quicker side of Good to Firm; monitor any late going stick movements.

Pearl River and Altareq both ran recently (11 and 6 days ago respectively) and both are natural prominent types who will find their path cramped early — watch how their jockeys (Hardie and Young) handle the first furlong in a field of 22.

races.name: John Smith's Stayers' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, sitting 14 days since last run and returning to a distance she has contested repeatedly in similar company; her Good to Firm going record is workable but her style-fit score reflects she may not be racing fully within her optimal role over this extended 2m½f — those who track her closely will be best positioned.
runners_data.comment: Rock N Roll Pinkie has been admirably consistent - 5th, 5th, 4th, 2nd, 6th in her last five - with today's trip and ground both proven. Tops our figures under 137 lb, though winless this spell and the yard is out of form (0/33).

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Irish raider who landed a 2m win on Good ground last time, boasting a strong trainer who is 3/14 in the last 14 days; likely to press close to the leader and has the form profile to stay every yard of this trip, but needs this pace to be genuinely honest to sustain his effort all the way.
runners_data.comment: Secret Force won last time out and again four starts back, with a third and fourth sandwiched in between. Already proven over today's going, he sits third on our figures under 133 lb and rates a leading threat back after 20 days off.

runners_data.name: Cruden
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished second five times from his last eight starts and clearly handles Good to Firm; Rossa Ryan takes the ride for a trainer in form (2/4 in 14 days) and his proximity-racing style will keep him involved, though he tends to be run out of it late rather than winning.
runners_data.comment: Cruden has been metronomically consistent - three seconds and two fifths in his last five - and already boasts form over today's trip. Second on our figures under 133 lb, he's a danger despite being winless in that sequence and having had 29 days off since.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Good ground recently and has course form at York; Jim Goldie saddles him in strong recent form (6/53 in 14 days) and Paul Mulrennan is an in-form booking, making him a credible prominent contender at a mark of 74.
runners_data.comment: Trojan Sun's only success this spell came two starts back, sandwiched by an 8th and 6th, though a 3rd four back shows he's capable of better. He has form over today's trip and going but sits only mid-pack on our figures (129 lb) after 17 days off.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Has won three of his last five over 2m on Good and Soft ground and is a genuine front-running type in terms of natural style — the field simply has too many horses seeking that territory, so he is likely to be pressed wider into the prominent-midfield band than he would prefer, which blunts his natural advantage slightly.
runners_data.comment: Treasure Islands has landed two of his last six starts, including one two starts back, and arrives with both today's trip and going already proven. Unplaced last time out, he sits mid-pack on our figures under 127 lb but is open to more once bounced back.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a recent win over 11f and a placed run over 2m, showing she stays well; Joanna Mason rides for a small trainer and ran only 7 days ago, but the horse's settling ability means she should travel comfortably off the pace and could produce a strong finish if the race is run at a controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Valley Of Flowers won last time out. A runner-up run three starts back adds to solid claims. With both today's trip and going already proven, she returns just seven days later under 126 lb and rates a leading threat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Terrorise
runners_data.note: Consistent but limited, with five of his last six runs on Good ground producing modest finishing positions; hold-up style suits this setup in theory but his form figures suggest he rarely finds enough when the race gets serious over staying trips — Brian Ellison's two-from-28 recent record tempers expectation.
runners_data.comment: Terrorise has struggled for his form - three unplaced efforts sandwiched by two 6ths in his last five - and remains winless in that sequence. He does have both today's trip and going proven, but sits only 7th of 11 on our figures under 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Soul
runners_data.note: Boasts four wins from his last five starts, all on Good or Good to Firm, and stays 2m-plus well having won over 20f; his true racing style is naturally prominent, but with the field packed up front he is likely to sit further off the pace here — if he settles and switches off, his class could be the telling factor in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Soul won last time out and again five starts back, either side of two 4ths and a 3rd - his form arrives in bursts. Both today's trip and going are proven, but he rates only 8th of 11 on our figures under a light 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Division Day
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with a win at 2m and a placed run at 2m4f, showing he stays genuinely; Warren Fentiman takes a 3lb claiming allowance which is significant at these weights, and 36 days since his last run leaves him fresh — his hold-up profile is genuinely natural and suits this scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Division Day boasts eye-catching recent form, winning three of his last five starts including two in succession, and has form over today's going. Yet he's our bottom-rated runner in this field of 11, and the yard is out of form (1/21) - hard to trust under 120 lb.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield due to the cluster of rear-runners in this field — form figures are uninspiring (no wins, no places in last five) and all five recent runs came on Good ground, suggesting the conditions are not the issue; Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps on paper but the form profile does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Furhaan has struggled for a placed effort lately - 5th, 7th, 9th, unplaced and 5th in his last five - and remains without a win in that sequence. He does have both today's trip and going proven, but sits only 9th of 11 on our figures under 118 lb.

runners_data.name: Queen Roslyn
runners_data.note: Another genuine hold-up type absorbed into midfield on the map because of the surplus of rear-runners; her best form has come on Soft and Heavy going (winner over 17f on Soft, placed over 20f on Soft), making this Good to Firm ground a clear concern — Brian Ellison's 1/20 recent record adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Queen Roslyn won twice in succession three and four starts back but has since faded to 5th and unplaced. She has both today's trip and going proven, but the yard is out of form (1/20) and she rates only 10th of 11 under 117 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Rock N Roll Pinkie is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger likely to push for the lead from the outset, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 2m½f trip on Good to Firm ground at York. The field contains a cluster of genuine prominent types — Treasure Islands, Cosmic Soul, and Cruden among them — but with more pace horses than the race shape can accommodate, several will be forced to settle off their natural position, reducing their effectiveness and concentrating tactical advantage in the hands of those who can dominate from the front or track the leader unopposed. Secret Force and Cruden will look to press close to Rock N Roll Pinkie and may apply brief pressure through the final mile, but the overall pace structure shapes up as measured rather than truly testing. This race shape most favours genuine hold-up or off-the-pace horses who can travel comfortably in behind a sustainable lead and produce a clean sustained finish from 3f out — horses like Valley Of Flowers, Division Day, and Cosmic Soul (if she settles better than mapped) are best placed to capitalise on a pace that is honest but unlikely to be truly searching. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural berth; Treasure Islands and Cosmic Soul are the most likely to actually press close to the pace, while Furhaan and Queen Roslyn will find themselves racing further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the field strings out conservatively behind her, allowing off-the-pace horses to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Rock N Roll Pinkie sets the fractions on her own terms with no rival willing to press, creating a pace that is steady enough to keep hold-up runners fresh for the final 3f; Valley Of Flowers, Division Day, and Cosmic Soul are best equipped to exploit this shape with a sustained run from midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Honest, Front Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie's gallop is genuinely strong on the fast ground and she builds a decisive lead that she never relinquishes.
scenarios.body: The Good to Firm conditions and a clear lead allow Rock N Roll Pinkie to control every second of the race, and any horse who travels prominently without burning energy early will be best placed; Secret Force and Cruden, who are likely to sit second and third, may be well positioned to challenge if the pace is truly honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crowded Midfield Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types all push forward early, creating a fractionally faster pace and bunching the midfield, causing tactical complications.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of Treasure Islands and Cosmic Soul into the midfield may generate traffic issues and interference entering the straight, and any horse who manoeuvres cleanly to the outside will have a significant advantage; Trojan Sun's prominent handler Jim Goldie has strong recent form and the horse already showed a win over this sort of trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sluggish Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a slow-motion procession and the race turns into a 2f dash to the line.
scenarios.body: A truly slow pace would compress the field and bring the sprinting sharp types into play over a trip where stamina normally dominates; this scenario is least likely given the honest pace tendency of York's flat track and the confirmed presence of Rock N Roll Pinkie.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Soul holds four wins from his last five starts including over 20f on Good ground — if he settles off the pace better than his natural style suggests and produces his stamina in the straight, he could be the classiest horse in the race at a lenient mark of 67.

Division Day claims a 3lb allowance through Warren Fentiman and has already placed over 2m4f; if the tempo is controlled and his hold-up run is clean, his improving profile at only 4 years old gives him a genuine winning chance that odds may not fully reflect.

The cluster of prominent types — Treasure Islands, Cruden, Secret Force and Rock N Roll Pinkie — will all be competing for early position and any jostling or shuffling in the first half-mile on a 2m½f trip could compromise those forced widest, particularly Treasure Islands who is most displaced from her natural role.

Queen Roslyn's form peak has come on genuinely soft ground and her last run on Good or better produced a 6th of 6; if the Good to Firm conditions strip her of any finishing speed, she is likely to be a non-factor despite her hold-up style theoretically fitting the scenario.

Trojan Sun is the only runner in the field combining a course win at York, a recent win on identical Good ground over 14f, and an in-form trainer-jockey combination — monitor his market move as a sign of confidence from the Goldie yard.

races.name: John Smith's Silver Cup Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Arabian Force
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with strong recent form (2nd-3rd-3rd) at 1m2f-1m4f in good going and solid going suitability (7/9 on similar ground); has 56 days between runs which may leave him short of peak sharpness, and despite being a natural front-runner he is likely to be pushed off his ideal position in this pace-compressed field.
runners_data.comment: Arabian Force remains without a win in his last five starts, but has been competitive with three thirds and two runner-up efforts, and carries an eye-catching speed figure of 105. races.paceDynamic: Peace Belle is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a six-runner field where every other runner is a genuine prominent type, she is highly likely to get an uncontested lead at a pace she controls entirely. The field is unusually pace-compressed: Arabian Force, Mount Atlas, Duke Of Oxford, Tabletalk, and Epic Poet are all naturally prominent horses, but there is only one front position and one true rail to settle behind, so several will be shuffled wider or deeper than they want. Peace Belle's last win came over 1m6f at York in good going — this exact conditions profile — and William Pyle can dictate a measured gallop that plays to her stamina, making the tempo a weapon rather than a test. With no credible hold-up horse in the field to generate a late surge, the race shape strongly favours a horse who can control pace and conserve energy through the middle portion, firing off the front in the straight — a profile that unambiguously suits a front-runner with course-and-distance form on fast ground. The field holds more prominent types than can realistically all secure their desired position; Peace Belle is almost certain to lead, with Tabletalk — highest-rated of the challengers and consistent over 1m4f-1m6f in good going — best placed to sit closest to the pace and mount the most dangerous challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Peace Belle Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Peace Belle secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a measured, sustainable gallop on this fast ground.
scenarios.body: She sets a controlled tempo through the back straight, conserving energy so that her stamina kick in the final two furlongs is decisive; with no natural hold-up horse to produce a late burst, rivals will struggle to pick her up if she has sufficient cover over them entering the straight.

scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Runs Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If the pace Peace Belle sets is just fast enough to stretch the field but not fast enough to secure her advantage, and a prominent stalker runs her down late.
scenarios.body: One of the true prominent types — most likely Tabletalk or Mount Atlas — sits a length or two off the leader, travels strongly through the race, and finds the energy to collar Peace Belle inside the final furlong on this ground that rewards relentless galloping; Tabletalk's consistency in similar conditions and strong RPR makes her the most credible threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.trigger: If Peace Belle goes off too fast relative to the field, the pace falls apart in the straight, and the horse best positioned to exploit it swoops.
scenarios.body: A horse that manages to settle just behind a hot pace — most likely Arabian Force or Epic Poet, though both are natural prominents pushed rearward by field dynamics — arrives with a run as the leader ties up; the danger here is that no true hold-up horse exists, so any late finisher is a prominent type under duress.

scenarios.label: D

scenarios.trigger: If prominent runners jostle for position early and disrupt Peace Belle's rhythm, creating a stop-start gallop with multiple pace changes.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early race suits the highest-rated and most experienced horse who can adapt, but with Peace Belle still likely to lead and Tabletalk well-handled by Rossa Ryan, the disruption is likely contained; Duke Of Oxford's consistent course form at 1m6f on Fibresand gives him a narrow angle if conditions go awry, though his going figures on turf are weak.

watchPoints.text: Peace Belle's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the pivotal factor — if she is allowed to set her own pace by a field of prominent types reluctant to commit early, she could prove very difficult to reel in over 1m6f on fast ground.

Tabletalk's prominent draw and Rossa Ryan's positive riding style mean he is most likely to sit closest to Peace Belle — watch whether he can get into that position at the start before Mount Atlas and Arabian Force crowd him out.

Arabian Force's 56-day absence is a fitness concern in a race likely to be run at a proper Group 3 tempo on fast ground; if he is not fully wound up, he may find the race ending before he gets into it, despite his strong form profile.

Epic Poet's redistribution to the rear of the pace map does not reflect his natural style — Daniel Tudhope will likely push him up earlier than the map suggests, and if he does manage to sit third or fourth, his vast experience at this course and trip makes him a factor in a messy race.

races.paceDynamic: Betties Bay is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine lead horse to pressurise her, she can dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good To Firm ground over York's straight six. The complication is that this field of 20 is loaded with prominent-racing types — Glory Hyde, Juan Les Pins, Havana Rum, Rock Opera, Fiscal Policy, Mister Sox and Ruby Red Gove all want to be in the first three or four, meaning the early positions will be fiercely contested even if the overall tempo is not truly blistering. Several horses labelled as midfielders — Kats Bob, Good Earth and Magic Boy — are natural prominent types who simply cannot all get their preferred position in a field this congested, so they will be pushed further back than ideal and their chances are consequently compromised. On balance, the race shape favours horses who can sit handy in the first quarter to half-dozen on a track where Good To Firm York six furlongs consistently rewards those who race prominently and travel sweetly into the straight without burning petrol.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Betties Bay Controls, Handy Types Strike

scenarios.body: Betties Bay sets a controlled, honest gallop and the race develops into a strongly-run but not suicidal affair, with the prominent handful immediately behind ideally placed rounding into the straight; those who can travel in the first six or seven are delivered to the business end with full tanks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Front Rail Burns

scenarios.body: With so many prominent types all seeking the same territory, the early exchanges become more pressured than Betties Bay would like, raising the sectionals and weakening those who fought for position; hold-up horses who get a true racing surface and a fast tempo to aim at come through late.

scenarios.body: A truly contested early gallop compresses the finishing positions and a horse who has been restrained off the pace gets a clean inside rail or open passage at the two-furlong pole; this is a low-probability shape because most of the supposed hold-up horses in this field are redistributed prominent types unlikely to be travelling easily in rear.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Solo Front Runner Rails
scenarios.trigger: If Betties Bay is allowed to dictate at a sedate tempo and the prominent cluster fails to mount a serious challenge, leaving the leader to score on the bridle.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace rival to force her hand, Betties Bay bowls along on her own terms on fast ground and the prominent types chase shadows in the straight; this scenario requires the rest of the field to be collectively flat or tactically slow to react, which is unlikely in a 20-runner sprint handicap.

watchPoints.text: Glory Hyde's in-form sequence (three wins from three) means she commands respect at the head of the prominent group — watch whether Joanna Mason gets her into a clean position behind Betties Bay in the first furlong, as traffic in a 20-runner field could be the one thing that derails her.

The cluster of prominent runners (Glory Hyde, Juan Les Pins, Havana Rum, Rock Opera, Fiscal Policy, Mister Sox, Ruby Red Gove) all wanting the same early ground means the draw and early positioning in the first furlong is critical — any horse trapped wide or squeezed back will find this race a lottery.

Betties Bay's true role as the race-controlling front-runner is important context — if she is crowded or bumped early by the prominent scramble, the entire pace dynamic changes and the hold-up horses gain a bigger chance than the headline shape suggests.

Educating Rita's 259-day absence is the standout fitness flag in the race — if she bounces back fresh she is interesting, but the risk of needing the run is high and players should monitor whether she is heavily supported or drifts in the market.

Yes I'm Mali finished second twice from six runs at this course and distance on Good To Firm — watch whether Daniel Tudhope angles her across to the far rail where the ground has been freshest all day, as York's track bias on fast ground can reward those who find the best strip.
